analysis.title: Bright Horizons Family (BFAM): Mixed 3Q as Full Service pressures offset Back-Up Care strength
key_insights: BFAM reported 3Q26 revenue of $841.5mn, up 4.8% y/y, in line with GS and slightly below FactSet consensus growth of 5.0%. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.4%, flat y/y, below GS 19.9% but in line with consensus. Adjusted EPS of $1.80 beat GS and consensus of $1.76.

Full-year 2026 guidance was lowered: revenue from $3.085-3.115bn to ~$3.07bn and EPS from $5.05-5.15 to $4.98-5.03. The cuts reflect softer Full Service enrollment and slower year-end Back-Up Care utilization as repeat users approach annual use-bank limits. GS says guidance points to negative consensus revisions.

Full Service revenue grew 1.3% y/y as tuition increases were partly offset by lower enrollment. Enrollment in centers open over one year fell ~50 bps y/y excluding Australia, with Australia adding ~100 bps of headwind. Occupancy was in the mid-60% range, flat y/y.

Net center closures reduced 3Q Full Service revenue growth by ~200 bps. BFAM closed 11 centers in 3Q (four in Australia), 42 year to date through September, with ~20 more planned for 4Q. The US will likely stay in net closure in 2027.

The UK regulator's group-wide safeguarding notice hurt fall enrollment more than BFAM expected, and a mid-September update extended the review. Enrollment pressure will be larger in 4Q and could persist until the notice is lifted, with limited visibility on recovery.

Australia continues to deteriorate on developer-driven capacity growth and softer demand, with occupancy at multiyear lows. It drove a $290mn goodwill impairment and a $4mn intangible impairment. BFAM is reviewing strategic alternatives with urgency, and GS sees a sale or exit as a way to improve the growth and margin profile and cut tax pressure from nondeductible losses.

Back-Up Care revenue rose 13.0% y/y on unique users and utilization, with penetration below 5% of eligible employees supporting the 11-13% long-term growth target. FY26 Back-Up Care growth guidance was lowered to ~13% from 13-15%.

Full Service operating margin fell 25 bps y/y to 3.7% but rose 40 bps excluding Australia, helped by tuition increases ahead of wage growth, efficiencies and center rationalization. BFAM expects Full Service operating margin up ~70 bps in 2026 excluding Australia.
Centers below 40% occupancy fell to 9% from 12% a year ago, while centers above 70% occupancy fell to 42% from 44% as preschool graduations outpaced new starts.

Educational Advisory revenue fell 2.4% y/y, slightly worse than GS estimate of -2.0%, on lower EdAssist participant utilization. FY26 guidance now assumes flat revenue versus prior low-single-digit growth.

GS cut 2026/2027/2028 revenue estimates to $3,071mn/$3,216mn/$3,465mn (average -1.5%) and EBITDA margins to 16.6%/16.9%/17.5%. EPS goes to $5.01/$5.93 for 2026/2027 and rises to $7.52 for 2028 from $7.46.

GS maintains Buy and cuts the 12-month price target to $80 from $93, based on 11.25x (14.0x prior) rolled-forward NTM+1YR EPS of $7.14. The multiple was lowered for reduced revenue visibility given Australia and the UK. Upside from $66.98 is 19.4%.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $80 from $93 on a lower target multiple of 11.25x versus 14.0x, reflecting weaker near-term visibility in Australia and the UK. Buy rating maintained.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported 10/29): revenue $841.5mn, +4.8% y/y, in line with GS est $841.6mn, below FactSet consensus growth of 5.0%.
3Q26 adjusted EPS $1.80 reported, vs GS est $1.76 and consensus $1.76; GAAP EPS was -$4.74 on a $290mn impairment and $27.4mn debt extinguishment and FX hedge loss.
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA $163.3mn, margin 19.4% flat y/y, versus GS est 19.9% and in line with consensus.
Segment growth y/y: Full Service +1.3% (GS est +1.0%), Back-Up Care +13.0% (in line with GS), Educational Advisory -2.4% (GS est -2.0%).

FY26 guidance lowered: revenue ~$3.07bn (prior $3.085-3.115bn), adjusted EPS $4.98-5.03 (prior $5.05-5.15). Before the print GS forecast revenue $3.10bn and EPS $5.12 versus FactSet consensus revenue $3.10bn and EPS $5.11.
GS new estimates: 4Q26E adjusted EPS $1.16 (prior $1.29), FY26E $5.01 (prior $5.12), FY27E $5.93 (prior $6.04), FY28E $7.52 (prior $7.46). 4Q26E revenue $738.1mn (prior $769.6mn), +0.6% y/y.
Revised FY26 guidance assumes Full Service growth of ~2% (prior 2.5-3.0%), Back-Up Care ~13% (prior 13-15%) and flat Educational Advisory.

tension_points.bull_case: Back-Up Care is growing 13% with penetration below 5% of eligible employees, underlying Full Service margin rose 40 bps excluding Australia, and a potential Australia exit would improve the growth and margin profile and reduce tax pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: Full Service enrollment is declining, ~20 more closures are planned for 4Q, UK regulatory review pressure will deepen in 4Q, and 2026 guidance was cut, pointing to softer near-term earnings growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The UK safeguarding notice staying in place with no recovery in family inquiries and new starts, or Australia occupancy showing no improvement.

theme_stances.key_argument: Weaker enrollment, continued center closures and reduced 2026 guidance point to softer near-term earnings growth.
